svg.title: Fig. 191 — The lituus r²θ = a²: the asymptote is the initial line; the sector OPA has constant area
svg.desc: Redrawn from Robert C. Yates, A Handbook on Curves and Their Properties (1947), Fig. 191, page 213. Section: spirals.

g.data-text: The pole O, the axes, and the asymptote, which is the initial line itself: as θ → 0 the curve runs out along it.
Take the angle θ and draw the ray OP at that angle from the initial line.
On the ray lay off r = a/√θ (θ in radians) to find P.
The circle about O through P meets the initial line at A. The sector OPA has the area r²θ/2 = a²/2, the same for every θ.
The branch r > 0: it comes in along the initial line from the right, and winds into the pole counter-clockwise.
The branch r < 0: the reflection of the first in the pole; it comes from the left along the initial line.
The book marks every place where the branches meet the axes.
